contentCodeableConcept.text: The patient reports a two-week history of central chest heaviness, precipitated by climbing three floors of stairs or walking briskly, radiating at times to the left arm as a dull ache, lasting four to five minutes and relieved by stopping and standing. One episode occurred at rest during an emotionally stressful phone call. Associated with exertional breathlessness and occasional sweating; no nausea or vomiting. He self-treated with Gelusil syrup twice without relief and took a single Dolo 650 for a headache. He denies fever, cough, giddiness or syncope; reports occasional palpitations.
Cardiovascular: exertional chest heaviness, occasional palpitations; no syncope, no pedal swelling
Respiratory: exertional breathlessness; no cough, no cold
General: no fever, no weight loss (gained 2–3 kg over the last year)
Genitourinary: nocturia once nightly; urine otherwise normal

Referral note to mention high occupational stress (accountant, ~10 h/day) and that the elder brother already has a coronary stent. Nocturia once nightly noted in the context of long-standing diabetes; urine microalbumin ordered to assess. The patient's presumed 'acidity' episodes are considered likely anginal in origin.
